A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same head-stylization framework, renamed from DiffStyle360 to StyleFusion360. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary materials are readable and support comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original FFHQ and RenderMe360 evaluations, component ablations, stylization–identity analyses, qualitative experiments, and a 15-participant user study.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark results, modulation ablations, expression-robustness and unseen-style experiments, runtime measurements, and a 50-participant user study.

M1.justification: V1 directly applies AdaIN to content keys using style keys before shared attention. V2 Section 3.2 introduces a trainable preliminary cross-attention stage with additional projections, then uses its output to modulate content keys through AdaIN. This substantially changes the central fusion mechanism. Local masks, style interpolation, and temperature scaling already existed in v1.

E1.justification: The training styles, FFHQ and RenderMe360 datasets, and head-stylization task remain. V2 expands unseen-style coverage with references such as crystal, cyberpunk, mushroom, and papercraft in supplementary Figure 5, and adds a controlled reference-expression variation scenario in main Figure 6.

E2.justification: V2 adds StyleID, StyleShot, and OmniStyle to the main quantitative and qualitative comparisons, substantially broadening the diffusion-based comparator set. StyleAligned also becomes an evaluated comparator in the component analysis. Identity3DHead matches v1's Bilecen et al., and DiffusionGAN3D matches its Diffusion3D row; those are naming changes.

E3.justification: The user study expands from 15 participants and 270 responses to 50 participants and 900 responses, retaining 18 questions per participant and the same holistic preference question. V2 adds runtime and peak-memory measurement protocols and a controlled expression-variation experiment. The stated training hyperparameters and synthetic-reference generation procedure remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 replaces v1's progressive component ablation with AdaIN/attention removal tests and adds key-only versus value-only versus joint modulation, expression robustness, and expanded unseen-style evaluation. V1's quantitative key-scaling sensitivity curves, detailed stylization–identity analysis, and illustrated eyebrow-consistency failure case are removed. These substantially change the questions investigated and supporting evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. Both principally report point estimates. The larger user-study sample changes evaluation sample size, without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains existing-baseline FFHQ scores but extensively revises RenderMe360 values: IP2P FID changes from 138.62 to 91.04 and depth error from 0.0261 to 0.0965. V2 replaces the two proposed-model rows with one and reports 76.0% user preference versus 78.2% under the smaller v1 study. It adds runtime, modulation, and unseen-style results while removing per-style CLIP/ID and key-scaling analyses. Changed models, sample sizes, and unexplained baseline-score revisions limit controlled before-and-after performance comparisons.

T1.justification: V2 Section 3.2 adds mathematical definitions for the secondary projections and cross-attention output Fcs, replacing AdaIN(Kc, Ks) with AdaIN(Kc, Fcs). The written value concatenation also changes from [Vl, Vs, Vc] to [Vl, Vc, Vs]. These are localized substantive formulation changes; neither version contains theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims of identity-preserving, view-consistent stylization without per-style retraining, unseen-style generalization, and local editing remain. V2 refines the claimed methodological contribution around learned, spatially selective content-key modulation. Local editing and intensity control receive greater prominence but were already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations based on soft content–style correspondences and interprets expression robustness as disentanglement. It newly qualifies applicability to references with human facial structures and acknowledges synthetic FID/CLIP targets as imperfect evaluation proxies. V1's detailed stylization–identity trade-off interpretation and discussion of rare cross-view eyebrow failures are removed, substantially revising the account of mechanisms and limitations.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a code-repository link and newly discloses training, dataset-generation, inference-stage, and peak-memory costs in supplementary Section 2.4 and Table 1. Existing disclosures—including the A100 GPU, 800 iterations, AdamW learning rate, 16-view batch, guidance weight, and default key-scaling value—are retained. These additions improve practical reproducibility information without establishing changed training settings.

R1.justification: V2 expands the style-transfer literature with works including StyTr2, AdaIN, StyleShot, and OmniStyle, while dropping references including B-LoRA and IP-Adapter. It more explicitly distinguishes its modulation from StyleAligned's global conditioning and adds animation-related future directions. The broader positioning around DiffPortrait360 and GAN-based head stylization remains.

P1.justification: Beyond renaming the framework, v2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, and method narrative. It incorporates the Style Appearance Module into the fusion subsection, promotes local stylization from experimental discussion to a method subsection, and substantially reorganizes the supplementary sections. This is extensive editorial and structural revision.

P2.justification: V2 switches from two-column to single-column presentation, redesigns the teaser and architecture diagram, expands the comparison display, and replaces several analytical figures with new ablation, expression, and generalization figures. Local-editing and interpolation displays are rearranged and combined. The training examples and final qualitative galleries are retained, including relocation into the reorganized supplement.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens assessment of the fusion mechanism through targeted controls and broader evaluated baselines, while making computational costs, facial-structure assumptions, and synthetic-evaluation limitations more explicit. These provide useful validation and transparency gains. Their overall benefit is tempered by removal of quantitative key-scaling trade-off evidence and the lack of explanation for substantial RenderMe360 baseline-score revisions, supporting a limited net improvement.
